Frequently asked questions

What is a boundary survey?

A boundary survey is a measured determination of the legal limits of a parcel of land, based on deed records, prior surveys and physical monuments recovered in the field.

How much does a survey cost?

Residential boundary surveys in our service area typically run between 1,200 and 3,500 dollars, depending on parcel size, terrain, and how much record evidence already exists.

Do I need a survey to build a fence?

If the fence goes near a property line, yes. Building a fence on the wrong side of a line is one of the most common causes of boundary disputes we are called in to resolve.

How long is a survey valid?

A survey does not expire, but the ground changes. Monuments get disturbed by construction and grading, so a survey older than about ten years is usually worth updating.
